entries.description: The Weasleys’ former Ford Anglia is described as running wild in the Forbidden Forest.
entries.model_notes: A mobile inhabitant of the Forest at this date, not a fixed parked vehicle or a constraint on the Forest’s dimensions.

entries.description: Hermione explains that Muggles see Hogwarts as a deteriorating ruin with an entrance warning declaring it dangerous and unsafe to enter.
entries.temporal: September 1994; described as an existing enchantment
entries.model_notes: Character explanation, attributed to her reading of Hogwarts: A History. This defines a Muggle-facing appearance; it does not establish that the actual castle is ruined. The subsequent Unplottability discussion concerns Durmstrang, not a confirmed Hogwarts property.

entries.description: The Hogwarts Express departs the concealed platform nine and three-quarters at King’s Cross, travels north, and arrives at Hogsmeade station after dark. The London platform is accessed through the apparently solid barrier between platforms nine and ten.
entries.model_notes: Regional approach context only. No travel distance or exact bearing beyond northward travel is given.

entries.description: At the stormy evening arrival, Hagrid waits at the far end of the platform. First-years traditionally sail across the lake to the castle; approximately a hundred apparently horseless carriages wait outside the station and carry the other pupils up a track towards Hogwarts.
entries.model_notes: Retain Harry’s perception of horseless carriages. The paragraph gives the upward route and approximate vehicle count, not the track’s measured length or the lake landing geometry.

entries.description: Carriages pass through gates flanked by winged-boar statues and climb a sweeping drive to the great oak front doors above a flight of stone steps. Many illuminated castle windows are visible through the rain.
entries.model_notes: Preserve the ordered station–gates–drive–steps–front-doors approach. No count of steps, gate material, or precise drive curvature is supplied.

entries.description: The Entrance Hall is cavernous and torch-lit and contains a magnificent marble staircase. Peeves hovers twenty feet above arriving pupils; water balloons leave the floor wet and slippery.
entries.model_notes: The hovering height supplies at least that much clearance at his position, not a measured ceiling height. Wetness belongs to this incident.

entries.description: Double doors on the right of the Entrance Hall lead into the Great Hall.
entries.model_notes: The right-hand relation is given on entering via the front doors; preserve that viewpoint.

entries.description: Hundreds of candles float above four long student house tables. Golden plates and goblets stand on the tables; at the top of the Hall the staff sit along one side of a fifth table facing the pupils. Harry’s route passes Slytherin, Ravenclaw and Hufflepuff before reaching Gryffindor at the far side, with Slytherin subsequently described across the Hall.
entries.model_notes: Record the observed traversal and opposite-side relation without assuming equal table spacing. The tablecloth is white linen; spilled pumpkin juice stains it during this meal.

entries.description: Flitwick sits on a large pile of cushions beside Sprout, who is beside Sinistra; Snape is on Sinistra’s other side. A vacant seat separates Snape from Dumbledore at the centre. The arriving Moody is given the seat on Dumbledore’s right, while Hagrid sits at an end of the table.
entries.model_notes: A dated seating arrangement. Harry guesses that the vacant seat is McGonagall’s; do not treat that identification as directly observed or fix all seating permanently.

entries.description: The enchanted ceiling shows the outdoor sky: swirling black and purple storm clouds and flashes of lightning. High dark windows admit the sound of heavy rain and shake with thunder.
entries.model_notes: Separate the magical visible sky from the actual roof structure, whose construction and height are not specified.

entries.description: The first-years line up along the staff table facing the rest of the school. McGonagall places the ancient patched Sorting Hat on a three-legged stool in front of them and removes both when the Sorting ends.
entries.model_notes: A removable start-of-term installation, not a permanent obstruction.

entries.description: Hagrid enters through a door behind the teachers’ table.
entries.model_notes: The door’s destination and dimensions are unstated; keep a usable connection without inventing its route.

entries.description: Dennis reports falling into the lake and being pushed back into the boat by something underwater. Colin suggests the giant squid; the narration describes the lake as fathoms deep.
entries.model_notes: The rescue is a character report; the squid identification is speculation. Fathoms deep is qualitative, not a mapped bathymetric measurement.

entries.description: Empty dishes fill with food without visible delivery. The first course vanishes and is instantly replaced by puddings, and remaining crumbs later disappear leaving clean plates.
entries.model_notes: Allow magical food-state changes at the tables. These paragraphs do not establish the mechanism or the kitchen’s position.

entries.description: Nearly Headless Nick reports that Peeves threw pots and pans around and left the kitchens flooded with soup before the feast.
entries.model_notes: A reported disruption earlier the same evening, not the normal kitchen state.

entries.description: Nearly Headless Nick says Hogwarts has over a hundred house-elves, normally in the kitchens by day, emerging at night to clean and attend to fires.
entries.model_notes: The stated count and work pattern are reported. They imply staffing and nighttime activity, not a proven kitchen capacity or plan.

entries.description: Dumbledore says the castle’s list of about 437 prohibited objects can be consulted in Filch’s office.
entries.model_notes: Provides a displayed or consultable office list; its mounting and format are unstated.

entries.description: Dumbledore reminds pupils that the Forest within the grounds is out of bounds and Hogsmeade is barred to pupils below third year.
entries.model_notes: Institutional access rules at this date, not an impassable physical barrier.

entries.location: Route to Gryffindor Tower: concealed staircase
entries.description: On the route from the Entrance Hall towards Gryffindor Tower the group passes through a door hidden behind a tapestry and climbs a narrower staircase. A step halfway up lets Neville’s foot sink through; a suit of armour at the top laughs, and Ron closes its visor.
entries.model_notes: No intervening route or floor number is given. The narration calls this one of many Hogwarts trick stairs; model this local trap without making every staircase identical.

entries.location: Gryffindor Tower entrance and common room
entries.description: A large portrait of the Fat Lady in pink silk hides the entrance. After the password she swings forward to expose a hole in the wall. The circular common room has a crackling fire, squashy armchairs, tables, and a doorway to the girls’ dormitories.
entries.model_notes: Password at this visit is Balderdash. Retain a climb-through wall opening and a separate girls’ dormitory doorway; the opening’s exact height is unspecified.

entries.description: A final spiral staircase reaches the boys’ dormitory at the top of the Tower. Five four-poster beds with deep crimson hangings stand against the walls, trunks at their feet. Bedside tables and headboards support Dean’s Krum and West Ham posters and Seamus’s Ireland rosette; warming pans have been placed in the sheets.
entries.model_notes: Specific to this dormitory and date. Harry attributes the warming pans to house-elves without witnessing placement; do not infer other dormitories’ bed counts.
